routes.label: Track the folded edges and find the height

question: A regular hexagon with sides of length \(6\) has an isosceles triangle attached to each side. Each of these triangles has two sides of length \(8.\) The isosceles triangles are folded to make a pyramid with the hexagon as the base of the pyramid. What is the volume of the pyramid?
solution:
Folding preserves the two \(8\)-unit sides of each triangular face. They become edges joining a common apex \(P\) to the six base vertices, so all six lateral edges have length \(8\).

Let \(O\) be the center of the regular hexagon. Joining \(O\) to consecutive vertices divides the base into six isosceles triangles with central angles \(360^\circ/6=60^\circ\). Each is therefore equilateral, so the distance from \(O\) to a vertex is \(6\). An altitude of one of these triangles bisects its base into two \(3\)-unit segments, giving altitude
\[
\sqrt{6^2-3^2}=3\sqrt3.
\]
Thus the base area is
\[
B=6\left(\frac12\cdot6\cdot3\sqrt3\right)=54\sqrt3.
\]
To locate the perpendicular height, let \(H\) be the foot of the perpendicular from \(P\) to the base plane. For any base vertex \(V\), the Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
HV^2=PV^2-PH^2=64-PH^2.
\]
Hence \(H\) is equidistant from all six vertices. Such a point must lie on the perpendicular bisectors of the base sides, whose intersection is \(O\). Therefore \(H=O\), and the positive height is
\[
h=PO=\sqrt{8^2-6^2}=2\sqrt7.
\]
A pyramid's volume is one third of its base area times its perpendicular height, so
\[
V=\frac13 Bh
=\frac13(54\sqrt3)(2\sqrt7)
=36\sqrt{21}.
\]
This is choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
